---
title: "Simulation parameters and results"
---

The time-domain solvers, [](`~slenderpy.cable.dynamic.solve`) and
[](`~slenderpy.beam.dynamic.solve_dynamic`), share the two classes of
[](`slenderpy.simulation`): [](`~slenderpy.simulation.Parameters`) describes
the run, [](`~slenderpy.simulation.Results`) holds what it produced.

## Parameters

```python
from slenderpy import simulation

parameters = simulation.Parameters(ns=101, t0=0.0, tf=60.0, dt=2e-3, dr=1e-2, los=[0.25, 0.5])
```

- `ns`: number of nodes of the space discretisation.
- `t0`, `tf`, `dt`: the time window and the time step. The run has
  `nt = round((tf - t0) / dt)` steps of `parameters.dt = (tf - t0) / nt`, the
  step actually used.
- `dr`: the output step. A snapshot is stored every `rr` steps, with `rr` the
  multiple of `dt` nearest to `dr`, `rr = round(dr / dt)`, kept within
  `[1, nt]`; the effective output step is `rr * dt`, and the last output may
  come slightly before `tf`.
- A `UserWarning` is raised when the effective time step or output step
  differs from the requested one.
- `los`: the positions where snapshots are stored, as **span fractions**
  (horizontal distance from support 1 divided by the span length), in
  `[0, 1]`; `0` and `1` are the supports. An integer `n` gives `n` evenly
  spaced positions, supports included.
- `pp`: show a progress bar.

The solvers always compute on the `ns` nodes; `los` only selects what is
stored, by linear interpolation between nodes.

## Results

A [](`~slenderpy.simulation.Results`) wraps an `xarray.Dataset` indexed by
`time` and `span_frac` (scalar variables, such as the number of Newton
iterations, only by `time`):

```python
res["z"].values          # array (number of outputs, number of positions)
res.lot(), res.los()     # output times, stored span fractions
res.state                # final state at full resolution, to restart a run
```

`drop` crops variables, positions or a time window in place; `dump` and
`load` save to and read from a file; `to_netcdf` and `to_json` export.

### The output contract

Every solver returns its results in one global frame: origin at support 1,
`x` along the span, `z` upwards, `y` completing a right-handed triad, SI
units.

| name | meaning | cable | beam |
|------|---------|-------|------|
| `x`, `y` | along-span and out-of-plane position (m) | yes | no |
| `z` | vertical position (m) | yes | yes |
| `vz` | vertical velocity (m/s) | no | yes |
| `curvature` | bending curvature (1/m) | no | yes |
| `moment` | bending moment (N.m) | no | yes |
| `eta` | Bouc-Wen internal variable | no | yes |
| `n_iter` | Newton iterations of the step (scalar) | no | yes |
| `dtension` | dynamic increment of axial force (N) | yes | no |

## Plots and spectra

[](`~slenderpy.simulation.multiplot`) draws one or several results on a
grid, one row per variable and one column per stored position.
[](`~slenderpy.simulation.spectrum`) returns the one-sided FFT modulus of
every variable as a new `Results` indexed by frequency, ready for
`multiplot(..., log=True)`.
